rationale: Direct experimental testing in human proband-derived cells demonstrates that while pathogenic variants in other MSL complex members (such as KAT8/MOF and MSL3 in Basilicata-Akhtar syndrome) produce a pronounced decrease in global bulk H4K16ac histone acetylation, patient-derived iPSCs carrying pathogenic de novo MSL2 variants maintain normal global bulk H4K16ac levels despite reductions in MSL2 protein levels. Consequently, unlike in MSL3- and KAT8-related syndromes, bulk H4K16ac biochemical assays cannot serve as a reliable diagnostic functional biomarker for Karayol-Borroto-Haghshenas syndrome, necessitating alternative molecular approaches such as specific peripheral blood DNA methylation episignatures.

evidence.text: In induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) derived from individuals with pathogenic MSL2 variants, MSL2 protein levels were diminished, but bulk global H4K16ac levels remained unchanged compared to controls, directly contrasting with variants in other MSL complex members (MOF and MSL3) which cause pronounced reductions in global H4K16ac.

new_directions.rationale: Patient iPSCs showed unchanged bulk H4K16ac by western blot or mass spectrometry, yet targeted dysregulation of MSL2 target genes was observed; ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN for H4K16ac in neural progenitor cells could reveal focal chromatin defects masked in bulk assays.

new_directions.question_text: Can peripheral blood DNA methylation episignatures reliably differentiate Karayol-Borroto-Haghshenas syndrome from Basilicata-Akhtar syndrome and KAT8-related syndromes in clinical cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Because bulk H4K16ac is uninformative for MSL2, clarifying whether the established blood DNA episignature has 100% specificity against other chromatinopathies within the MSL and NSL complexes is essential for frontline differential diagnosis.
